LUMETIS has recently been selected to reach the lunar incubation programme called “TechTheMoon” thanks to strong perspectives of its patented technologies for human and robotic exploration. 
One of our most noteworthy results is the invention and development of a fluorescence and reflectance hyperspectral imaging system reaching unprecedented spectral range (300 nm – 1000 nm) and sensitivity. Besides, LUMETIS has demonstrated being able to acquire fluorescence images of rocks, plants and contaminations on sensitive surfaces outside dark conditions of laboratories and therefore allowed the exploration of new technical and scientific fields. Last but not least, we have imagined and set up a multispectral (8 wavelengths) high resolution demonstrator for art applications. 
LUMETIS employs technologies invented by its founders within CNES and CNRS ecosystems. Some of the inventions were patented for space applications, improved for art applications and will be made even more outstanding before going back to space.

The company is established with the primary objective of transferring and disseminating technological innovations to the agricultural sector to promote sustainable agriculture models.
Specifically, the company aims to develop the use of remote sensing as an information framework for operating agricultural machinery equipped with Variable Rate Technology (VRT), as well as to provide technology transfer services. These services encompass the acquisition, processing, and distribution of data derived from remote sensing, advanced sensor systems, and IT infrastructure to business entities—including agricultural enterprises, machinery manufacturers, agricultural contractors, and producers' associations—for precision and sustainable agriculture applications.
The company's activities include support actions (dissemination, demonstration, training, system design, technical consultancy) aimed at implementing a georeferenced information service platform. entityDescription:
LGr Technologies AS is a Norwegian deep-tech SME based in Trondheim, developing modular, lightweight sensor systems for situational awareness in harsh and remote environments.
The company's core products are MLTS (Mobile Lightweight Tactical Sensor), a rapidly deployable perimeter sensor node that can be carried and installed by a single person and operates unattended for up to two weeks (approximately eight days at -30 degC), and Heimdall, a command-and-control software platform that fuses data from distributed MLTS nodes into a single real-time situational picture. A third system, Munin, a semi-autonomous human-in-the-loop UAV platform that responds to a triggered MLTS node with live thermal imaging, is under development.
Core technical competences include low-power embedded sensor electronics, edge processing and sensor fusion, resilient communication between distributed nodes over low-bandwidth and intermittent links, and operator-centred software for sensor networks. The systems are designed for robustness in Arctic and subarctic conditions, autonomy under severe energy constraints, modularity and scalability - design drivers shared with space and remote-asset applications.

entityDescription: Founded in 1975, the Institute of Environmental Physics conducts research in a field that emerged in the 1950s from the development and application of nuclear physics measurement methods to study the Earth's climate and environmental system. Today, its scientific mission as a branch of physics encompasses questions that investigate the flow of energy and matter in our environment. Research areas include the physics and chemistry of the atmosphere, greenhouse gases, and remote sensing (Prof. André Butz), as well as aquatic processes and the Earth's climate history (Prof. Werner Aeschbach and Prof. Norbert Frank). The measurement and simulation of the radiative impact of aerosols in the climate system (Prof. Stephanie Fiedler). Image processing in the environmental sciences takes place at the Interdisciplinary Center for Scientific Computing at the University of Heidelberg (Prof. Carsten Rother, em. Prof. Bernd Jähne), and remote sensing of the atmosphere is carried out at the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry in Mainz (Prof. Thomas Wagner). Research into aerosols is carried out at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Prof. Thomas Leisner). Further links exist with the Klaus Tschira Laboratory for Physical Age Determination (KTL), a facility of the Curt Engelhorn Center for Archaeometry (CEZA) and the Curt Engelhorn Foundation.

entityDescription:
Materia Nova is a non-profit applied research centre in materials science and process engineering based in Mons, Belgium, founded by the University of Mons. With more than 330 collaborative and industrial R&D projects, it takes technologies from laboratory proof of concept to pilot and demonstrator scale (TRL 2 to 6).
Its multidisciplinary teams cover polymers and composites (bio-based resins and biopolymers, bio-based flame retardants and fire testing, advanced recycling, reactive extrusion, electrospinning); surface engineering and thin films (PVD, PECVD, atmospheric plasma, ion implantation, plasma treatment and spheroidisation of powders for additive manufacturing); wet-chemistry coatings and electrochemistry (sol-gel, electroplating, chemical metallisation, electrolytes and electrocatalysis); gas sensors and electronic noses; and industrial biotechnology (fermentation, biomethanation, bioelectrochemical systems, enzymatic recycling, CO₂ utilisation).

The Nauka. To Lubię Foundation is a Polish non-governmental organization established in August 2020 and based in Gliwice. It was founded by Dr. Tomasz Jan Rożek, a physicist, science journalist, and popularizer of science, to develop educational, multimedia, and science communication initiatives.
Mission and Objectives
The Foundation promotes science, technology, digital skills, and education, with particular attention to supporting families. Its main objectives are to:
- develop future skills and critical thinking among children and adults;
- promote digital hygiene and media literacy;
- strengthen resistance to misinformation, cyber threats, and scientific disinformation;
- support equal access to education;
- provide free, high-quality educational materials to schools, underserved regions, and Polish communities abroad.
Scale and Impact
The Foundation operates throughout Poland and internationally through digital platforms, social media, and educational events.
Between August 2020 and January 2026, its three YouTube channels generated more than 97 million views, 8.7 million hours of watch time, and over 886,000 subscribers. The Foundation’s social media community exceeds 600,000 followers, while its website attracts approximately 3,000 users per week.
The organization also regularly hosts a popular science stage during the annual science festival in Katowice, connecting experts from various fields with tens of thousands of visitors.
Key Projects
Academy of Superheroes is a long-term project presenting Polish scientists as real-life heroes in order to inspire young people. It has distributed 15,000 free books to primary schools, while its animated series has received more than 220,000 views. The project also includes multilingual educational games and e-books.
Digital Parent Academy is an online educational platform for parents and teachers. It offers free webinars, articles, and expert materials on digital hygiene, screen-time management, online privacy, FOMO, and internet safety.
Micrometeorite Hunters is a nationwide science education program combining astronomy and environmental studies. Under teacher supervision, students search for cosmic dust and analyze air pollution. Participating schools receive free research kits, including microscopes, magnetic detectors, and educational guides.
Cosmic Week is a free interdisciplinary campaign focused on space exploration. It has engaged more than 30,000 students across Poland and provides teachers with ready-to-use lesson plans and educational materials.
Partnerships
The Foundation works with universities, scientific institutions, companies, public organizations, and social partners. Its cooperation includes developing educational programs, organizing science events, implementing social campaigns, and distributing free educational resources.
One campaign promoting Polish science reached more than one million passengers nationwide.

The National Museum of Natural History Goulandris is a non-profit foundation with a mission to conduct research, provide education, and protect nature. entityDescription:
Hydra Manufacturing Limited is a private company limited by shares, incorporated in England and Wales (company number 15939081), based at Nexus, Discovery Way, Leeds, LS2 3AA, United Kingdom. It is a deep-tech spinout from the University of Leeds, engaged in the production and sale of ceramic manufacturing equipment and ceramic components.
Hydra develops and commercialises CHAMP, a hybrid additive and subtractive manufacturing platform for high-performance technical ceramics. CHAMP combines layer-wise deposition with in-process machining and closed-loop, AI-assisted defect detection and correction, producing near-net-shape ceramic parts with accuracy and surface quality that conventional ceramic additive routes cannot reach without extensive post-processing. The platform is designed, built and programmed in-house across mechanical design, motion control, firmware, process software and materials formulation, so Hydra holds the full technical stack for its own product. The process has been demonstrated in alumina, hydroxyapatite, reaction-bonded silicon carbide and tungsten carbide cobalt chrome, with monolithic silicon carbide in development and AI defect control validated on alumina through doctoral and Innovate UK funded work. These materials and the associated geometric freedom apply directly to space hardware such as thermal protection structures, optical and structural substrates, propulsion components and wear-critical mechanisms, where low volumes make tooling-dependent ceramic routes prohibitive on cost and schedule.
Under Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC Hydra is a micro-enterprise: three full-time staff and one part-time employee at 0.4 FTE (3.4 annual work units), with turnover well below the relevant threshold. It has no subsidiaries, holds no participation in any other undertaking and is not a subsidiary of any organisation.
Issued capital is 1,143,236 shares across two classes carrying identical voting, dividend and capital rights. The three full-time executive officers, all co-founders, hold 57.3 per cent between them; founder and employee shareholders hold 78.7 per cent in total. The University of Leeds retains a founder stake of 8.7 per cent, and 12.5 per cent is held by nominees acting for two SFC Capital managed funds. No shareholder or group of connected shareholders holds 25 per cent or more of the capital or voting rights, so Hydra is an autonomous enterprise.
The board comprises Matthew Shuttleworth, Louis Masters, Daniel Davie, Robert Kay and Luke Watson, chaired by Keith Jackson, and is responsible for supervision, management and day-to-day administration. Investors hold conventional minority protections: one non-executive appointment right, a non-voting observer, quarterly reporting and reserved matters covering corporate actions such as changes to share capital or the nature of the business. These do not reach operational, technical or engineering decisions. Hydra holds its own premises, employs its own staff, owns its own equipment and contracts in its own name, and is not subject to direction by any parent or controlling entity.
All foreground intellectual property, including the CHAMP platform design, control software and materials formulations, is owned by Hydra. University of Leeds background IP is held royalty-free under agreement, with full assignment to Hydra after a two-year term, giving unrestricted exploitation rights over its core technology.
Hydra supplies capital equipment through the CHAMP X3 platform alongside a manufacturing-as-a-service offering. Its first production system has been sold to Lucideon, a UK materials technology organisation. The company is backed by pre-seed equity through the SFC Capital funds and competitive Innovate UK grant funding. Target sectors are aerospace, space and defence, with ISO 9001 certification on the near-term roadmap.

entityDescription:
Theia Sense is an early-stage deep-tech company developing advanced fiber optic sensing systems for structural health monitoring (SHM) in harsh and extreme environments, with a primary focus on space applications.
The company specializes in Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG)-based sensing technologies, combined with proprietary packaging solutions that enable the measurement of mechanical parameters beyond conventional capabilities, including shear stress, which is typically not accessible with standard FBG sensors.
Theia Sense’s approach integrates hardware and software into a unified platform, including optical sensors, space-compatible packaging, interrogation systems, and data processing tools aimed at enabling real-time monitoring, diagnostics, and predictive maintenance of critical structures.
The technology is designed to operate in demanding conditions such as vacuum, radiation, thermal cycling, and high-vibration environments, making it suitable for spacecraft structures, launch systems, and advanced composite materials.
The company is currently focused on ground validation and early-stage system development, with the objective of progressing towards in-orbit demonstration and space qualification. Theia Sense leverages strong links with research and industrial partners in the aerospace sector and builds upon expertise in photonics, materials engineering, and sensor integration.

entityDescription:
The Linesmen and Boatmen National Association of the Italian Ports (ANGOPI) is the trade association which represents the linesmen and boatmen interests at the international, national and local level in a unitary way. In particular the ANGOPI defends the linesmen and boatmen profession through the unity, the connection and the coordination of the associated Groups.
It promotes the recognition, at normative and organizational level, of the mooring and of the boating as a service of general interest useful for the safety of navigation in ports and the safety of landing. It promotes, as well, the organizational models provided for every ports at national level, which ensure each linesmen and / or boatmen Group the function of universal service provider.
· It represents, in a unitary way, the linesmen and boatmen interests at national and at local level: in particular, during the investigation aimed to determine the organization and discipline of the Groups, the public service obligations and the tariffs.
· It protects and develops the associated Groups general interests about economic, organizational, administrative, legal, tax issues, anyway connected to their activity.
· It contributes to the creation and regulation of new working relationships and collaboration between associated Groups and third parties, where it is recognizable also a more general interest of all members in the protection of the category. 
· It takes care of the members professional development and of the Groups growing qualification, through the study of the problems concerning the category.
· It stipulates with the trade unions representing the employees the Category National Collective Agreement on behalf of the linesman and/or Boatmen Groups. With trade unions defines tools for the professional growth of the category and for the its welfare.
· It provides, to the associated Groups, all possible assistance and general and/or particular advice that they need.
· It advances and develops proposals to set up the method for the service tariffs and in general to make proposals for legislation and administration acts to be submitted to the competent authorities.
· It designates, where relevant, their representatives in all the committees in which the Association is involved in its own or is invited in accordance with specific laws or other measures taken at national or local level by the competent authorities, as well as in the commissions for the public examination provided to enter into the profession, so that also from the Association the highest contribution in the technical selection of candidates is guaranteed;
· It promotes, and if necessary manages, initiatives to establish and regulate relations of cooperation and friendship between the Association and boatmen Associations from other countries.
· With regard to the initiatives above mentioned, the Association has exclusive competence both with respect to individual Groups, and with respect to individual linesman / boatmen with particular regard to those who can produce effects modifying the organizational model of the mooring/boating service;
